name: Common Cold
description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat. Usually clears up on its own within a week.
advice: Rest, fluids, and over-the-counter cold medicine. See a provider if symptoms last beyond 10 days.

care.instruction: Schedule a visit at Student Health Services this week.

name: Seasonal Flu
description: A viral infection that hits harder and faster than a cold, often with sudden fever and exhaustion.
advice: Rest and fluids for most cases. Seek care quickly if you're high-risk or symptoms worsen after a few days.

name: Fever (Unspecified)
description: A temperature above normal, usually a sign the body is fighting something off.
advice: Monitor temperature and stay hydrated. Seek care if fever exceeds 103°F or lasts more than 3 days.

name: Migraine
description: A recurring, often one-sided headache that can come with light sensitivity and nausea.
advice: Rest in a dark quiet room and stay hydrated. See a provider if this is a new or unusually severe headache.

description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually from a virus, causing stomach upset.
advice: Stay hydrated with small sips of water or electrolytes. Seek care if you can't keep fluids down for 24 hours.

name: Mild Allergic Reaction
description: A localized immune reaction to something like pollen, food, or a skin irritant.
advice: An antihistamine usually helps. Watch closely for any trouble breathing or swelling of the face or throat.

name: Anaphylaxis (Severe Allergic Reaction)
description: A life-threatening allergic reaction that can close the airway within minutes.
advice: Use an epinephrine auto-injector if available and call 911 immediately. Do not wait to see if it improves.

care.instruction: Call 911 or get to the ER immediately. Do not drive yourself if symptoms are severe.

name: Asthma Attack
description: A flare-up that narrows the airways, making it hard to breathe normally.
advice: Use a rescue inhaler if prescribed. If it isn't helping or lips/fingertips turn blue, this becomes an emergency.

advice: Call or text 988 right now, or reach campus counseling's crisis line. You deserve support today.
